title: ci-cd-rollback-breadcrumbs-notes-7
content:
Notes / breadcrumbs for the canary rollback on 2024-11-03 (personal scratchpad)

Background:
- Canary rollout for service 'router-api' started 2024-11-03 09:05 PST (image: router-api:v2024.11.03-482).
- Target was 10% traffic for 1 hour, automated checks enabled (latency SLO + error-rate guardrails).
- At ~09:30 PST alerts triggered (5xx increase) on canary instances.
- Immediate mitigation: paused rollout, started investigation, then rolled back to v2024.10.29-451 to restore baseline.

What I did (commands + outputs tried while investigating):
1) Check k8s rollout status (cluster: prod-west, namespace: router):
- kubectl --context=prod-west -n router rollout status deployment/router-api-canary
  -> "Waiting for rollout to finish: 1 old replicas are pending" (09:26)

2) Inspect pods + logs for canary pods:
- kubectl -n router get pods -l app=router-api,track=canary -o wide
  -> 3 pods (node-12, node-15, node-18), RESTARTS: 0, READY: 1/1
- kubectl -n router logs router-api-canary-5f8d7 -c router-api --since=30m\  (snippet)\  -> ERROR: failed to initialize model cache: timed out after 10s\  -> WARN: connection pool exhausted, dial tcp 10.12.0.23:6379: i/o timeout

3) Check config differences between canary image and stable:
- docker run --rm router-api:v2024.11.03-482 env | grep -i redis  (local quick check from image registry)\  -> REDIS_HOST=redis-cluster.prod-west.internal\  -> REDIS_CONN_TIMEOUT=10000
- docker run --rm router-api:v2024.10.29-451 env | grep -i redis\  -> REDIS_HOST=redis-cluster.prod-west.internal\  -> REDIS_CONN_TIMEOUT=5000

Hypothesis: increased connection timeout in new image config + event loop changes cause more simultaneous redis connections -> connection pool exhaustion under canary traffic pattern. Also saw model cache init timeout that may cascade to 5xx.

4) Checked infra alarms and redis metrics around 09:20-09:35:
- redis average connections spiked from 120 -> 210 (baseline 100-130).
- CPU on redis-primary stable; network spikes on node-12 where one canary pod sits.

5) Artifact/versioning notes:
- Canary image tag: router-api:v2024.11.03-482 (PR #482) introduced async initialization + new connection pool code (author: @diego).
- Rollback performed to router-api:v2024.10.29-451 (PR #451) which had synchronous init and older pool behavior.
- Confirmed image digests:
  - v2024.11.03-482 -> sha256:aa11bb22cc33\  - v2024.10.29-451 -> sha256:dd44ee55ff66

6) Reproduce attempts in staging:
- Deployed canary image to staging (staging-west) with same 10% traffic config; hit with synthetic traffic (ab) to simulate load. Observed similar redis connection exhaustion and model init timeouts.

Error snippets collected:
- "failed to initialize model cache: timed out after 10s" (router-api stderr)
- "dial tcp 10.12.0.23:6379: i/o timeout" (go net)
- "pool get: no available connections" (redis client)

Quick timeline (notes):
- 09:05 rollout started
- 09:18 first anomalies in tracing (increased db/redis latency)
- 09:22 error pages observed by synthetic monitors
- 09:30 on-call paused rollout and rolled back 09:36

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Rolled back canary to stable image (kubectl set image deployment/router-api router-api=router-api:v2024.10.29-451)
- Re-routed traffic, resumed baseline and confirmed error rate back to normal by 09:50

Root-cause hypothesis (working):
- PR #482 changed initialization semantics -> async init spawns N goroutines during start which briefly spike redis usage/connections while warming model cache; combined with larger connection timeout and pool misconfiguration leads to transient exhaustion under canary traffic.
- Secondary contributor: client-side retry/backoff absent in some code paths -> retries amplify load on redis during init spikes.

Open questions / next steps:
- Confirm with Diego exact pool config changes in PR #482 (max open, idle, dial timeout). (ACTION: @Diego to paste pool config)
- Add connection metrics (pool.available, pool.in_use) to router-api metrics before next canary. (ACTION: create small PR to instrument)
- Add synthetic warmup traffic during canary rollout to avoid cold-init spikes. (ACTION: runbook change)
- Consider lowering default REDIS_CONN_TIMEOUT or adding exponential backoff on init. (ACTION: assign to eng-serving-runtime)

Notes for rollback checklist (to make future rollbacks smoother):
- Always include image digest in rollback ops to avoid tag drift. (we used tag; check digests in registry)
- Have playbook commands for both kubectl and helm environments. Example: helm rollback router-api 3 --namespace router; kubectl rollout undo deployment/router-api --to-revision=451
- Ensure observability dashboard has a "canary-init" pane showing pool metrics, model-init times, and redis connections.

Scratch TODOs (personal):
- Draft quick postmortem skeleton for owner @diego (include timeline, mitigation, RCA, follow-ups).
- Open follow-up card in JIRA (JIRA-RELE-217) linking to this doc + PR #482.
- Coordinate with infra to check node-12 network flakiness around 09:20 (possible unrelated noise).

Random notes / hypotheses to validate later:
- Could be a retry storm from upstream LB during canary rollout (some clients don't respect 429/503 and hammer). Check client logs for retry patterns.
- Check whether new image changed keepalive/tcp settings that could affect connection reuse.

If I forget: next immediate step is to get Diego to confirm config + add minimal pool metrics before re-attempting a canary.

End of scratchpad.
